t: You're on London Road in Southwark, a short street linking St George's Circus to the Elephant and Castle roundabout. To the east is the London South Bank University campus, including the Technopark and London Road buildings, and at the southeastern end sits Elephant and Castle tube station. The poet Eliza Cook was born here in 1818. She was known for her belief in self-improvement through education, which she called levelling up, and she was hugely popular with working class readers in England and America. She also argued for political freedom for women.
